name: Carbon laser peel (Hollywood peel)

lead: The carbon laser peel is a short clinic treatment where a carbon lotion is applied to the face and laser pulses are passed over it. It is offered for smoother texture and a brighter look.
It is marketed as the Hollywood peel for its quick pre-event glow.

paras: The carbon lotion is said to absorb laser energy, exfoliating surface skin and debris. Specific published trials of the procedure are not available.
Laser resurfacing can cause redness, pigment changes, and in rare cases scarring or acne and herpes flares.

lead: The carbon laser peel, often marketed as the Hollywood peel, is a clinic laser treatment aimed at smoother skin texture, smaller-looking pores and a brighter complexion with little downtime. A carbon-based lotion is applied to the face and then treated with laser pulses; the lotion is said to absorb the energy and lift debris and surface skin.

Laser resurfacing as a category is described as controlled wounding that prompts skin to regenerate, with heating of the deep dermis stimulating fibroblasts to form new collagen and elastin, and with ablative (CO2, Er:YAG), non-ablative and fractional devices [1]. Chemical peels, by comparison, range from light alpha- and beta-hydroxy acid peels used for fine lines, uneven pigment and acne to medium and deep peels with more discomfort and recovery [2]. The specific carbon-lotion procedure has no published trials identified, and the sources describing it are clinic descriptions rather than studies.

paras: Practitioners describe the treatment as a carbon lotion plus laser session, with a brief appointment and quick return to normal activity. Laser resurfacing in general ranges from ablative lasers like CO2 and Er:YAG to non-ablative and fractional devices.[1]

Wikipedia notes that, in resurfacing generally, devices are chosen by depth of effect: ablative lasers vaporise tissue and create wounds, while non-ablative lasers keep the skin intact and fractional lasers treat pinpoints and leave healthy skin between them [1]. The carbon peel is promoted as sitting at the gentle end of this range, with a quick return to normal activity.
No studies found. Related research on laser resurfacing and chemical peels is described generally in medical references.[1][2]

Laser resurfacing in general carries risks of scarring, hyperpigmentation, acne flares and herpes outbreaks.[1] Chemical peels can cause redness, pigment changes and photosensitivity, rising with depth.[2]
It is discussed alongside other skin-texture treatments, with popular interest tied to celebrity-style red-carpet skin.

Light chemical peels are described as treating fine wrinkles, dryness, uneven pigment and acne, usually with only slight stinging, redness and dryness afterwards [2]. Medium trichloroacetic acid peels are done in a clinic or outpatient surgery centre and cause more discomfort, and the article states that the deeper the peel, the more complications can arise [2].
